title: Standard Error of the Mean (SEM)

references.label: General microbiology/quantitative methods references (ASM, FDA BAM)

explanation: Estimates how much a sample mean is expected to vary from the true population mean, based on the sample's standard deviation and sample size. Unlike standard deviation, which describes the spread of individual data points, SEM describes the expected precision of the mean itself and shrinks as more replicates are added — it is commonly used for error bars on replicate-averaged data, distinct from standard deviation error bars which describe raw data spread.

variables.meaning: Number of observations/replicates in the sample

workedExample.scenario: A measurement repeated in triplicate (n = 3) with a sample standard deviation of 0.6.

commonMistakes: Reporting SEM when standard deviation (the actual spread of the raw data) is what the reader needs, or vice versa, without stating which is shown.
Calculating SEM from a very small n (e.g. n = 2), where the estimate is unstable and easily misleading.
Assuming a smaller SEM by itself means the underlying measurements were more accurate, when it may simply reflect a larger n.
